build: PAL original, two-sided G64; level 1 load in play

comments.text: Entry of the level 6 file. Jumps to the main loop at $1EFF, which runs the setup $51F7 and then repeats from $1F02: the disabled check $65E4, the object scan $0F69, the energy bar $578E, the check $1F63, the trigger $1F6A, the banner step $56A5, the score $5842, the timer $7BBB and $7B1B and the pause check $74B1. The loop starts again at $1EFF after the continue screen, and ends through the sound silence $B828 and a jump to the resident loader at $0404.
The NMI handler (the setup $51F7 points the NMI vector $FFFA/$FFFB here): saves A, sets the NMI flag $0A2B to 1, restores A and returns with RTI. The main loop reads the flag at $1F54.
Set to 1 by the NMI handler at $0A23; cleared by the setup $51F7 and read by the main loop at $1F54.
62 zero bytes between nmi_flag ($0A2B) and slot_frame ($0A6A) ($0A2C-$0A69), no reader.
Sprite pointer value of each slot, 14 bytes ($0A6A-$0A77); written by $1076 and $1DF5 and by the behaviours, and copied by $66D5 into the pointer tables.
Sprite colour of each slot, 14 bytes; written by $1DF5 and the behaviours and copied to $D02A-$D02E by $66D5.
1 when a slot's sprite is multicolour, 14 bytes; set by $1DF5 and the behaviours and copied into $D01C by $66D5.
Animation counter of each slot, 14 bytes; counted down by the behaviours $1524, $16BA and $1BBE as their frame counter, and stepped up 0 to 7 by $15C6 as its direction; cleared by $7A84.
Walk phase of each slot, 14 bytes, which picks the frame from the tables read by $1DF5; cleared by $1076 when it hits.

Walk counter of each slot, 14 bytes: the walking behaviours $185C and $1AA1 set it to half a random byte when it is zero and move the slot only while it is non-zero; nothing counts it down in the traced code. Cleared by $7A87.
Hurt timer of each slot, 14 bytes: set to 10 by $1076, counted down by the walking behaviours $185C and $1AA1 (which do nothing else while it runs), and cleared by $7A8A.

State of each slot (14 bytes, of which the first 11 are used): 0 free, otherwise the type copied from $0B26 by $0F69; the state picks the behaviour in the table at $124F. $1076 sets 1 or 2 on a hit and $61BC sets $10; the walks $185C and $1AA1 turn it between 1 and 2 and start the attacks 15 and 14, which return it to 1 and 2, $548E sets $18, $54F9 sets $17 and $62C2 restores the state saved in $0B6C. 7 is handled by $1DF5.
76 zero bytes between slot_state ($0ACC-$0AD9) and obj_type ($0B26) ($0ADA-$0B25), no reader.

Type and state of each of the 70 objects; 0 means no object, and the value is copied into the slot state $0ACC when the object takes a slot. Copied from $7649 by $7A1D; $61BC sets $10, and the code that changes a slot's state writes it here too: the walks $185C and $1AA1 (2 and 1), $548E ($18), $54F9 ($17) and $62C2 (the restored state).

Counter of each object, used by the behaviours as a timer, step or saved state; copied from $768F by $7A1D, cleared by $1076 on a hit, and set by $61BC to the slot's old state (the entry after the object, $0B6D, is set to $FE).
Flag of each object; copied from $76D5 by $7A1D and used by the behaviours.
Energy of each object (hits it can take), counted down by $61BC; copied from $771B by $7A1D.

Variant flag of each object, 0 or 1 (a second set of frames); copied from $7761 by $7A1D and read by $1076, $1DF5, $61BC, the walks $185C and $1AA1, the attacks $1726 and $196C, $6271, $62C2 and $9382.
A second flag of each object; copied from $77A7 by $7A1D, and $1076 sets a non-zero one to 2 when the object is hit.

Left limit of the object's walk, low byte; copied from $77ED by $7A1D and read by $1076 and $185C. Other behaviours use it otherwise: $1524 as the upper height, $54F9 as the height it restarts from, and the shot $146C as its direction, which the attacks $1726 and $196C write two entries on ($0CCC).
Left limit of the object's walk, high byte; copied from $7833.
Right limit of the object's walk, low byte; copied from $7879.
Right limit of the object's walk, high byte; copied from $78BF.
World X of each object, low byte; copied from $7905 and kept up to date by the behaviours and by $1076 (which also writes the entry after the hit object).
World X of each object, high byte; copied from $794B.
World Y of each object, low byte; copied from $7991.

World Y of each object, high byte; copied from $79D7. $1F6A writes 3 into the entries of objects 41 to 44, and $93AF adds 1 to the 16-bit Y of objects 52 and 53 each frame while its fall timer runs (the carry from $0EA2/$0EA3 reaching their entries here).
The object each of the slots holds (14 bytes), set by $0F69, cleared by $7A1D and read by $11D8, $1DF5 and the player's blocking tests $80AF and $8118.

The slot each object holds, for the 70 objects; set by $0F69 (which reads it back to release the slot) and cleared by $7A1D. $1DF5, $80AF and $8118 read it one entry back ($0F07,Y) for the slot of the previous object.
20 zero bytes between obj_slot ($0F08-$0F4D) and scan_dx_lo ($0F62) ($0F4E-$0F61), no reader.
Scratch of $0F69: the object's X minus the camera X, low byte.
Scratch of $0F69: the object's X minus the camera X, high byte.
Scratch of $0F69: the object's Y minus the camera Y, low byte.
Scratch of $0F69: the object's Y minus the camera Y, high byte.
Short hop for the object scan: the beq at $0F6E (an object of type 0) cannot reach the release code at $0FF7, so it lands here and jumps there. Reached only from scan_objects ($0F69).

Scans the 70 objects, last to first (X from $45), against the camera ($CB/$CC across, $D9/$DA down). An object with type $0B26 of 0, or outside the window (from 26 pixels left of the camera to less than $015A right of it, and $14 to $D6 below the camera's top) is released: if it holds a slot, that slot's state $0ACC is cleared, its height $CD,X is set to $FE and the object's flag $101A is cleared. An object inside the window that has no slot takes the first free slot of the 11 ($0ACC zero), which gets the object's X and Y in $79/$B1 and $95/$CD and its state from the type, and $0EFA and $0F08 link slot and object; the whole scan ends if no slot is free. Called once per pass by the main loop at $1F05.
Holds the object index saved by $0FFC: the immediate operand of the LDX at $100C.
1 for each object that holds a slot, 70 bytes; set and cleared by $0F69 and cleared by $7A1D.
20 zero bytes between obj_active ($101A-$105F) and hit_flag_a ($1074) ($1060-$1073), no reader.
Set to 1 by $1076 when it lands a hit, which makes further calls of $1076 return at once; cleared by the player state routines.
Set to 1 by $1076 on a hit, with $1074; $61BC reads it to take 2 instead of 1 from the object's energy.

For slot X (object Y), tests whether the player's punch or strike hits it. It returns at once when a hit was already scored this frame ($1074 or $1075 set), when neither the punch timer $5C48 nor the strike timer $5B3D is running, or when the slot's state $0ACC is not 1, 2, 14 or 15; the slot's screen height $A3,X must be at most $17 lines above or 9 lines below the player's $7B17 and its screen X within 25 pixels in front of the player's $7B16, on the side given by the facing $59CA. On a hit it pushes the object 9 pixels along the map in that direction unless it is already at its limit ($0D56/$0D9C to the right, $0CCA/$0D10 to the left), copies the new X to the slot and to the next object too, sets the slot to state 1 (player facing right) or 2 (facing left) with a frame in $0A6A that depends on the variant $0C3E, starts the hurt timer $0ABE with 10, sets $1074 and $1075 and calls $61BC. Called by $11D8 for each slot that is not in state 7, until the raster reaches line $B4.
Number of state 7 slots queued in $11CA by $11D8.
List of the slots in state 7 found by $11D8 (ended by $FF), handled after the others by $1DF5.
2 zero bytes between slot_queue ($11CA-$11D5) and update_objects ($11D8) ($11D6-$11D7), no reader.

Per-frame object update, skipped while the game is paused ($6449). Goes through the 11 slots: a slot in state 7 is only queued in the list at $11CA (count in $11C9); for the others, while the raster is above line $B4, it runs the hit test $1076 and then the behaviour for the slot's state, through the table at $124F and a call whose operand is rewritten at $1223/$1224, with the slot's object in Y and in $124E. The list is ended with $FF and each queued slot then goes through $1DF5. Called by the top interrupt at $654F.

Low byte of the address in the JSR at $1222 (high byte at $1224), rewritten by $1216 and $121C with the behaviour for the slot's state from the table at $124F; the $128B (behave_free) the file holds is only a placeholder.
Holds the queue index saved by $1239: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1247.

The object of the slot being handled by $11D8 (the Y register for the hit test and the behaviours), kept here because the table lookup at $1211 uses Y; $11D8 reloads Y from it at $121F, and the behaviours $134B, $1BBE, $1CDE and $54F9 read it back after using Y for a table.

Table of 30 behaviour routines, one word each, indexed by the slot state in $0ACC: 0 $128B behave_free, 1 $185C behave_walk_left, 2 $1AA1 behave_walk_right, 3 $1BBE behave_energy_pickup, 4 $1C7C behave_score_pickup, 5 $1CBE behave_flash_frame, 6 $1CDE behave_lobbed_shot, 7 $1DF5 slot_follow, 8 $1E9F behave_none, 9 $16BA behave_flashing_hazard, 10 $1524 behave_vertical_patrol, 11 $15C6 behave_radial_shot, 12 $14FF behave_colour_6, 13 $150A behave_colour_1, 14 $196C behave_attack_right, 15 $1726 behave_attack_left, 16 $6271 behave_knocked_down, 17 $146C behave_enemy_shot, 18 to 22 $5471 to $5475 behave_none_18 to behave_none_22, 23 $548E behave_falling_object, 24 $54F9 behave_falling_burst, 25 $1416 behave_light_start, 26 $1439 behave_light_blink, 27 $13E5 behave_follow_object_y, 28 $13AF behave_map_switch, 29 $134B behave_drop_rise. $11D8 copies the word into the operand of the call at $1222.
Behaviour for state 0 (entry 0 of the table at $124F): a lone RTS, so a slot in state 0 does nothing.

95 pairs of bytes read by behaviour $134B, indexed by the object's counter $0B6C (steps of 2, up to $BC): the sprite pointer $0A6A and a signed number of lines added to the slot's Y. Pairs 0 to 6: pointer $6A, 0 lines; 7 to 10: $6A, 4 lines down; 11 to 18: $6A, 3; 19 to 26: $6A, 2; 27 to 34: $6A, 1; 35 to 93: $6B and $70 alternating every second pair, 1 line up; 94: $70, 5 lines up. The lines down and the lines up each add up to 64. The last byte ($134A, $FF) is not read.

Behaviour for state $1D (entry 29 of the table at $124F), the type of objects 58 to 63 of the table at $7649. Makes the slot multicolour ($0A86) with colour $0B ($0A78) and runs the contact test $53D7: on contact it calls $5449 to hurt the player. It then adds 2 to the object's counter $0B6C (back to 0 at $BE) and reads the pair of bytes at that index in $128C: the first is the sprite pointer $0A6A, the second a signed number of lines added to the slot's Y ($95/$CD) and written to the object ($0E6E/$0EB4). So over 95 frames it waits 7, drops 64 lines and rises the same 64 lines again.
Scratch of $134B: for a negative step of the table $128C, the step with its sign removed, which is then subtracted from the slot's Y ($95/$CD).

Behaviour for state $1C (entry 28 of the table at $124F), the type of object 57 of the table at $7649. Makes the slot single-colour ($0A86 = 0) with colour 1 ($0A78). While the object's energy $0BF8 is non-zero it shows pointer 0 and returns. Otherwise it shows pointer $67 and runs the contact test $53D7: on contact it sets the object's energy to 1, calls $1EF2 with A=0 (which writes 0 into the four level map bytes that the setup $51F7 filled with 1), sets the banner flag $56A1 to 1 and the banner timer $56A2 to $C8, which starts the banner.

Behaviour for state $1B (entry 27 of the table at $124F), the type of objects 52 and 53 of the table at $7649, the two that $93AF moves down at the end of the level. Copies the object's Y ($0E6E/$0EB4) to the slot's Y ($95/$CD) and leaves the slot's X alone. Makes the slot multicolour with colour $0B and picks the pointer: for an object whose flag $0BB2 is zero $CB, or $CC once the finale flag $621F is set, and for one whose flag is non-zero $CD. Only the table at $124F reaches it: the RTS at $13E4 before it is the end of the previous routine.

Behaviour for state $19 (entry 25 of the table at $124F). While the flag $51F6 is zero it runs the contact test $53D7 and on contact sets the flag to 1; the LDA #$09 at $1427 is overwritten by the next instruction. The slot is always multicolour ($0A86) with colour 6 ($0A78) and pointer $70. No object in the table at $7649 has type $19.

Behaviour for state $1A (entry 26 of the table at $124F). Makes the slot single-colour with colour 1 and pointer $FC. While the flag $51F6 is non-zero it counts the slot's phase $0AA2 down from $0D to 0 (restarting at $0E) and takes pointer $FC for phases below 7 and $FD for 7 and up, so the shape changes every 7 frames. No object in the table at $7649 has type $1A.

Behaviour for state $11 (entry 17 of the table at $124F): the shot of a walking enemy, the object two entries after the one that fires it (objects 6, 9, 12, 19, 26 and 56 of the table at $7649). Makes the slot multicolour with colour $0B and pointer 0 (nothing to see). While the object's counter $0B6C is zero it only copies the X of the object two before it ($0DE0, $0E26) to this object and to the slot. The attacks $1726 and $196C set the counter to $32; the shot then counts it down, runs the contact test $53D7 (on contact it calls $5449 and clears the counter) and moves the slot 5 pixels a frame right with pointer $73, or left with pointer $74 when $0CCA of the object is non-zero (the attacks set $0CCC for it). It clears the counter when the slot has left the screen.
Behaviour for state 12 (entry 12 of the table at $124F): only makes the slot multicolour ($0A86) with colour 6 ($0A78); the pointer stays as it was. No object in the table at $7649 has type 12.
Behaviour for state 13 (entry 13 of the table at $124F): only makes the slot multicolour ($0A86) with colour 1 ($0A78); the pointer stays as it was. No object in the table at $7649 has type 13.
Sprite pointers of behaviour $1524: $68 seven times and $69 eight times, indexed by the slot's $0A94 (14 down to 0), so it shows $69 for eight steps and then $68 for seven.

Behaviour for state 10 (entry 10 of the table at $124F). Makes the slot multicolour with colour 0, counts its $0A94 down from 14 to 0 (a value of $0F or more, or 0, restarts at $0F) and takes the pointer from the table $1515 by it. It then moves the slot 2 lines a frame between two heights: with the object's counter $0B6C at 0 it goes up until its Y ($95/$CD) equals the pair $0CCA/$0D10 and sets the counter to 1; with the counter at 1 it goes down until Y equals $0D56/$0D9C and sets it to 0. The new Y is written to $0E6E/$0EB4. There is no contact test. No object in the table at $7649 has type 10.
Holds the Y register saved by $1541: the immediate operand of the LDY at $154B, which gives Y back after the table lookup.

The eight steps of behaviour $15C6, 4 bytes each (X change low and high, Y change low and high, 16-bit and signed), chosen by the slot's $0A94: up (0,-4), up and right (4,-4), right (4,0), down and right (4,4), down (0,4), down and left (-4,4), left (-4,0), up and left (-4,-4).
The step that $15C6 has chosen, copied from $15A2: X change low and high, Y change low and high, added to the slot's X ($79/$B1) and Y ($95/$CD).

Behaviour for state 11 (entry 11 of the table at $124F). Makes the slot multicolour with colour $0B and pointer $67 and runs the contact test $53D7: on contact it calls $5449 and restarts at $1635. Otherwise, while the object's counter $0B6C is non-zero, it counts it down and adds one of eight steps to the slot's position (the table $15A2, chosen by the slot's $0A94, copied to $15C2-$15C5). At $1635 it sets the counter to $1E, steps $0A94 on (0 to 7) and puts the slot at the position of the object before this one ($0DE1, $0E27, $0E6D, $0EB3). So it starts from the object before it every 31 frames (30 frames of flight and one to restart) and flies 4 pixels a frame in the next of eight directions. No object in the table at $7649 has type 11.
Holds the Y register saved by $15ED: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1614, which gives Y back after the table lookup.

The 90 sprite pointers of the flashing hazard of behaviour $16BA, indexed by the slot's counter $0A94: $6F ten times, $6E ten times, $6D sixteen times, $6E three times and $6F three times (42 steps with a picture), then 48 zeros for which the behaviour skips the contact test. The two zero bytes after it ($16B8-$16B9) are not read.
2 zero bytes between flash_frames ($165E-$16B7) and behave_flashing_hazard ($16BA) ($16B8-$16B9), no reader.

Behaviour for state 9 (entry 9 of the table at $124F), the type of objects 47, 50 and 64 of the table at $7649. Makes the slot multicolour ($0A86) with colour $0B ($0A78), counts its counter $0A94 down from $59 to 0 (a value of $5A or more, or 0, restarts it at $59) and takes the sprite pointer $0A6A from the table $165E by that counter, so the hazard shows for 42 of every 90 steps. When the pointer is not zero it runs the contact test $53D7, and when that returns non-zero it calls $5449 to hurt the player. It does not move the slot.
Holds the Y register saved by $16D7: the immediate operand of the LDY at $16E1, which gives Y back after the table lookup.

Returns A=1 when slot X is at or to the right of the player on the screen (its screen X high byte $BF,X is non-zero, or its screen X $87,X is not below the player's $7B16) and A=0 when it is to the left. Called by the walking behaviours $185C and $1AA1 (at $1921 and $1B65).

Returns A=0 when slot X is about level with the player and A=1 when it is not: the slot's screen height $A3,X is compared with the player's $7B17, and the answer is 0 when they are equal, when the slot is less than 10 lines above the player and when it is less than $1C lines below him. Called by the walking and attack behaviours ($17B0, $1891, $19F6 and $1AD6).

Hit recoil counter, counted down by $6313; while it is running (and $5447 is zero) the joystick bytes $1FA4/$1FA5 are not refreshed, so the direction that an attack forced stays. $5449 sets it to 3 and the attacks $1726 and $196C to 4; irq_top keeps the player's sprites 0 and 1 white while it is non-zero.

Behaviour for state 15 (entry 15 of the table at $124F): the attack of a walking enemy that faces left, entered from $185C with the object's counter $0B6C at $19. Calls $9382 first and makes the slot multicolour. By the variant $0C3E it writes the frames and distances into six operands of its own code ($1788, $1790, $179F, $17A7, $1803, $1817; variant 1 in brackets). At counter 0 it returns to state 1. Counting down: at 4 frame 5 ($14) and 8 (6) pixels right; at $0E frame 7 ($17) and 6 (0) pixels left, and if the player is level ($1704) and up to 27 pixels left of the slot it forces the joystick left ($1FA4), sets the recoil $1725 to 4 and calls $5456; if the object's flag $0BB2 is set it clears it and starts the shot two objects on (counter $32, X of the slot, direction $0CCC set to 1); at $12 it moves 2 (6) pixels left and sets the phase $0AA2 to 2; at $18 it takes frame 5 ($14).
Frame (sprite pointer) that $1726 gives the slot when its counter reaches 4: the operand of the LDA at $1787, set to 5 or, for variant 1, $14 at $1756 and $1735.
Distance in pixels that $1726 moves the slot right when its counter reaches 4: the operand of the ADC at $178F, set to 8 or, for variant 1, 6 at $175B and $173A.
Frame (sprite pointer) that $1726 gives the slot when its counter reaches $0E: the operand of the LDA at $179E, set to 7 or, for variant 1, $17 at $1760 and $173F.
Distance in pixels that $1726 moves the slot left when its counter reaches $0E: the operand of the SBC at $17A6, set to 6 or, for variant 1, 0 at $1765 and $1744.
Distance in pixels that $1726 moves the slot left when its counter reaches $12: the operand of the SBC at $1802, set to 2 or, for variant 1, 6 at $176A and $1749.
Frame (sprite pointer) that $1726 gives the slot when its counter reaches $18: the operand of the LDA at $1816, set to 5 or, for variant 1, $14 at $176F and $174E.
Sprite pointers of the walk to the left for variant 0: $05 eight times, $06 eight times, and the same again, indexed by the phase $0AA2 (0 to $1F); read by behaviour $185C.
Sprite pointers of the walk to the left for variant 1: $14 eight times, $15 eight times, and the same again, indexed by the phase $0AA2 (0 to $1F); read by behaviour $185C.

Behaviour for state 1 (entry 1 of the table at $124F): an enemy walking left. Calls $9382 first; the slot is multicolour with colour 9. When the object's second flag $0C84 is neither 0 nor 2 it only shows the standing frame $05 ($14 for variant $0C3E non-zero) and returns. Otherwise, with $0A10 zero and the player level ($1704) and up to 26 pixels left of the slot, it starts the attack: state 15, counter $0B6C $19. While the hurt timer $0ABE runs it only counts it down. If the object two on has type $11 and a zero counter ($0B6E), the slot is on screen at a height of $64 to $BD and a random byte ($65C4) is below $14, it sets the flag $0BB2 and attacks too. At its left limit ($0CCA/$0D10) it turns to state 2. When the walk counter $0AB0 is zero it takes half a random byte and turns when the slot is left of the player ($16F3); otherwise it moves 1 pixel left (X $79/$B1, also written to this object and the next) and steps the phase $0AA2 through 0 to $1F for the frame from $181C (variant 0) or $183C.

Behaviour for state 14 (entry 14 of the table at $124F): the attack of a walking enemy that faces right, entered from $1AA1 with the object's counter $0B6C at $19. The same as $1726 the other way round: it calls $9382 first, writes frames and distances into six operands of its own code ($19CE, $19D6, $19E5, $19ED, $1A48, $1A5C; variant 1 in brackets) and at counter 0 returns to state 2. At 4 frame 2 ($10) and 8 (6) pixels left; at $0E frame 4 ($13) and 6 (0) pixels right, and if the player is level and up to 27 pixels right of the slot it forces the joystick right ($1FA4), sets the recoil $1725 to 4 and calls $5456; a set flag $0BB2 starts the shot two objects on with direction 0; at $12 it moves 2 (6) pixels right and sets the phase $0AA2 to 2; at $18 it takes frame 2 ($10).
Frame (sprite pointer) that $196C gives the slot when its counter reaches 4: the operand of the LDA at $19CD, set to 2 or, for variant 1, $10 at $199C and $197B.
Distance in pixels that $196C moves the slot left when its counter reaches 4: the operand of the SBC at $19D5, set to 8 or, for variant 1, 6 at $19A1 and $1980.
Frame (sprite pointer) that $196C gives the slot when its counter reaches $0E: the operand of the LDA at $19E4, set to 4 or, for variant 1, $13 at $19A6 and $1985.
Distance in pixels that $196C moves the slot right when its counter reaches $0E: the operand of the ADC at $19EC, set to 6 or, for variant 1, 0 at $19AB and $198A.
Distance in pixels that $196C moves the slot right when its counter reaches $12: the operand of the ADC at $1A47, set to 2 or, for variant 1, 6 at $19B0 and $198F.
Frame (sprite pointer) that $196C gives the slot when its counter reaches $18: the operand of the LDA at $1A5B, set to 2 or, for variant 1, $10 at $19B5 and $1994.
Sprite pointers of the walk to the right for variant 0: $02 eight times, $03 eight times, and the same again, indexed by the phase $0AA2 (0 to $1F); read by behaviour $1AA1.
Sprite pointers of the walk to the right for variant 1: $10 eight times, $11 eight times, and the same again, indexed by the phase $0AA2 (0 to $1F); read by behaviour $1AA1.

Behaviour for state 2 (entry 2 of the table at $124F): an enemy walking right, the mirror of $185C. Calls $9382 first and makes the slot multicolour with colour 9; with the object's second flag $0C84 neither 0 nor 2 it only shows the standing frame $02 ($10 for variant 1). With $0A10 zero and the player level ($1704) and up to 26 pixels right of the slot it starts the attack: state 14 with the counter $0B6C at $19; the same random shot test as $185C can start it too. At its right limit ($0D56/$0D9C) it turns to state 1. When the walk counter $0AB0 is zero it takes half a random byte and turns when the slot is right of the player ($16F3); otherwise it moves 1 pixel right and steps the phase $0AA2 through 0 to $1F, taking the frame from $1A61 (variant 0) or $1A81.
Sprite pointers of behaviour $1BBE: $62 seven times and $63 seven times, indexed by the slot's $0A94 (11 down to 0); the last two bytes are never read.

Behaviour for state 3 (entry 3 of the table at $124F): a pickup that gives energy (object 69 of the table at $7649). Makes the slot multicolour with colour 2. When the object's energy $0BF8 is non-zero (taken) the pointer is 0 and nothing else happens. Otherwise the pointer comes from $1BB0 by the slot's $0A94 (11 down to 0) and the slot bobs: the object's counter $0B6C steps by 2 round the 24 heights of $1C4C, which are added to the slot's Y and written to $0E6E/$0EB4. On contact ($53D7) it sets the object's energy to 1, adds $0A to the player's energy $5448 (at most $21) and plays sound effect 4 (X = $10) through $B0EE.
Holds the Y register saved by $1BEB: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1BF5, which gives Y back after the table lookup.
Holds the Y register saved by $1C3F: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1C47.
Holds the X register saved by $1C3C: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1C49.

The 24 heights of the bobbing of behaviour $1BBE, signed 16-bit values added to the slot's Y each frame, chosen by the object's counter $0B6C (steps of 2): 0, 0, -1, -1, -2, -2, -3, -3, -2, -2, -1, -1 and the same with the opposite signs, so the pickup rises 18 lines and comes back.

Behaviour for state 4 (entry 4 of the table at $124F): a pickup that gives points (objects 65 to 68 of the table at $7649). Makes the slot multicolour with colour 3. When the object's energy $0BF8 is non-zero (taken) the pointer is 0; otherwise it is $6C and the contact test $53D7 runs: on contact the object's energy becomes 1, 5 is added to score digit 4 through $5816 (500 points, going by the digit positions described there) and sound effect 3 (X = $0C) plays through $B0EE.
Holds the X register saved by $1CA2: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1CAC.
Holds the Y register saved by $1CB1: the immediate operand of the LDY at $1CB9.
Holds the X register saved by $1CAE: the immediate operand of the LDX at $1CBB.

Behaviour for state 5 (entry 5 of the table at $124F). Makes the slot multicolour with colour 9; while the object's counter $0B6C is non-zero it counts it down and shows pointer $6B, otherwise pointer $6A. This routine never sets the counter; the type 6 behaviour $1CDE sets the counter of the object before it to 7 when it restarts, so a type 5 object placed just before a type 6 one would flash each time that one restarts. No object in the table at $7649 has type 5 or 6.

Behaviour for state 6 (entry 6 of the table at $124F). Makes the slot multicolour and runs the contact test $53D7: on contact it calls $5449 and restarts at $1D54. Otherwise colour 2 and pointer $67; the object's counter $0B6C, stepped each frame, runs through the table $1D89: from 4 to $33 the slot moves 4 pixels left, and each table value of $5A or more is a sprite pointer while a smaller one is added to the slot's Y (written to the object too). At $6A, or on contact, $1D54 clears the counter, sets the counter of the object before it ($0B6B) to 7, and puts the slot and the object $16 pixels left of and 1 line above that object.

106 bytes read by behaviour $1CDE, indexed by its counter after the step (1 to $69, so byte 0 is never read), and by $54F9 from $1DBD. A value of $5A or more is a sprite pointer, a smaller one a number of lines added to the slot's Y. Indexes 0 to 3: pointers $7B, $7C, $7B, $7C; 4 to 13: 0; 14 to 51: 0 to 5 lines, growing; 52 to 105: the burst frames $72 (6), $71 (6), $64 (5), $65 (5), $66 (5), $64 (5), $65 (5), $66 (5), $71 (6), $72 (6).
The frame limit that $1DF5 compares the previous slot's frame with: 5, or $14 for variant $0C3E non-zero.
1 zero byte between follow_limit ($1DF3) and slot_follow ($1DF5) ($1DF4), no reader.

Behaviour for a slot in state 7 (entry 7 of the table at $124F), run by $11D8 after the other slots with the slot in X and its object in Y. Makes the slot multicolour ($0A86) with colour 9 ($0A78) and copies the object's position ($0DE2/$0E28 across, $0E6E/$0EB4 down) to the slot ($79/$B1, $95/$CD). It then picks the sprite pointer $0A6A from the slot of the previous object ($0F07,Y): from the table at $6241 by that slot's phase $0AA2 when it is in state $10, otherwise from $1E7F when its frame is below the limit in $1DF3 (5, or $14 for variant $0C3E non-zero) and from $1E5F when not. Probably the lower sprite of a two-sprite enemy that follows the upper one.
Sprite pointers $0C, $0D, $0E and $0F, eight each, indexed by the phase $0AA2 of the previous slot: the frame $1DF5 gives a state 7 slot when the previous slot's frame is at or above the limit $1DF3.
Sprite pointers $08, $09, $0A and $0B, eight each, indexed by the phase $0AA2 of the previous slot: the frame $1DF5 gives a state 7 slot when the previous slot's frame is below the limit $1DF3.
Behaviour for state 8 (entry 8 of the table at $124F): a lone RTS, so a slot in state 8 does nothing. No object in the table at $7649 has type 8.

Low byte of the 16-bit sum camera X ($CB/$CC) minus $86 plus the player's screen X ($7B16), stored by the code at $7A9C; read by the trigger $1F6A, the finale step $93AF and the player states (at $5AB5, $5AD9, $5C82, $5CCC, $5E34, $5E64, $5F8F and $5FBF).
High byte of the 16-bit map position whose low byte is $1EA0; read by $1F6A, $93AF and the player states (at $5AB0, $5AD2, $5C7D, $5CC5, $5E2F, $5E5D, $5F8A and $5FB8).
Shapes of the digits 0 to 9, 8 bytes each; $5855 and $7B43 copy them to the panel, and $9670 swaps them with the block at $C450.
Writes A into four bytes of the level map, at $852F, $856F, $85AF and $85EF (64 bytes apart). Called by the setup $51F7 at $530A with A=1 and by the behaviour $13AF at $13D7 with A=0.

The level's main loop. It runs the setup $51F7, then from $1F02 on every pass the disabled check $65E4, the object scan $0F69, the energy bar $578E, the check $1F63, the trigger $1F6A, the banner step $56A5, the score $5842, the timer $7BBB and $7B1B and the pause check $74B1. It then shows the ending screen $75EA and leaves when the ending flag $6220 is set, or when $0A11 is set and the key code $6618 is $20; when the energy $5448 is zero (and $0A11 is clear) it shows the game over screen $587B and, when $0A12 (the credits) is not zero, the continue screen $9494, which sends the loop back to $1EFF if fire was pressed ($9493); and when the NMI flag $0A2B is set it shows the game over screen and leaves. It leaves through SEI, the sound silence $B828 and a jump to the resident loader at $0404.
Reads the energy $5448 and then branches to the next instruction whichever way it comes out ($1F66 is a bne to $1F68), and returns, so it has no effect. Called by the main loop at $1F0B.
Set to 1 by $1F6A when it has fired, so that it runs only once; cleared by the setup $51F7. The player code at $5D64 also reads it: down on a map byte $0D sets player state 4 only while it is 0.

Runs once (flag $1F69): when the player's map position $1EA1/$1EA0 is below $010A and the camera height $DA/$D9 is below $0113, it sets $1F69 to 1 and writes 3 into the high Y byte ($0EDD to $0EE0) of objects 41 to 44. Returns at once otherwise. Called by the main loop at $1F0E.
Horizontal fine scroll (6 at the start), ORed into the low bits of $D016 by the top interrupt $6486.
Vertical fine scroll (6 at the start), ORed into $D011 by the top interrupt $6486.
1 zero byte between scroll_y_fine ($1FA2) and joystick ($1FA4) ($1FA3), no reader.

Joystick port 2 ($DC00) as last read by $6313; bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire, clear when pressed. $FF at the start; $93AF overwrites it with $F7 or $FF during the finale, and the enemy attacks at $17D1 (left pressed) and $1A16 (right pressed) overwrite it when they hit the player, starting the recoil $1725 that stops $6313 reading the port.
CIA 1 port B ($DC01) as last read by $6313.
Cleared by the setup $51F7 ($5293); nothing in the traced code reads it.
Which of the two screen matrices is on show: 0 selects $CC00 and 1 selects $C800 (through $62FD); the scroll routines build the other one and flip this at the end. Cleared by the setup.
The camera height low byte ($D9) as scroll_step ($1FAC) saved it at $1FB4.
The camera height high byte ($DA) as scroll_step ($1FAC) saved it at $1FB9.
The camera X low byte ($CB) as scroll_step ($1FAC) saved it at $1FBE.
The camera X high byte ($CC) as scroll_step ($1FAC) saved it at $1FC3.

Called by the bottom interrupt $63EE unless the banner flag $56A1 is set. While the game is paused ($6449) it only reads the keyboard through $6619 into $6618. Otherwise it saves the camera ($CB/$CC across, $D9/$DA down) in $1FAA/$1FAB and $1FA8/$1FA9 and the player's screen position in $5934/$5935, then either goes on with the scroll in $206E for the steps left in $206F, or picks a new direction from the player's screen position: right at X $DC or more, left below $64, up above Y $41 and down at $87 or more (corners combine them), stores it in $206E, sets $206F to $0B and clears $2070 and $2EC4. The scroll routine for the direction comes from the table at $2075 through a call whose operand is rewritten at $2064/$2065; a frame with no scroll to make reads the keyboard instead.
Low byte of the address in the JSR at $2063 (high byte at $2065), rewritten by $205A and $2060 with the scroll routine for the direction from the table at $2075.
Scroll direction chosen by $1FAC (0 none, 1 down, 2 up, 4 right, 5 right and down, 6 right and up, 8 left, 9 left and down, 10 left and up).
Frames of scrolling still to run for the direction in $206E; set to $0B when a scroll starts and counted down by $1FAC. Cleared by the setup.
Phase 0 to 3 of the scroll step, advanced by $1FAC each frame; picks which part of the screen shift the scroll routines do.
2 zero bytes between scroll_phase ($2070) and scroll_spare_a ($2073) ($2071-$2072), no reader.
Cleared by the setup $51F7 ($52D2 and $539E); nothing in the traced code reads it.
Cleared by the setup $51F7 after scroll_spare_a ($2073); nothing in the traced code reads it.

Table of 16 routine addresses indexed by the scroll direction in $206E times 2: 1 down $2626 (scroll_down), 2 up $29BF (scroll_up), 4 right $20C8 (scroll_right), 5 right and down $323C (scroll_right_down), 6 right and up $2D14 (scroll_right_up), 8 left $341E (scroll_left), 9 left and down $308C (scroll_left_down), 10 left and up $2EC5 (scroll_left_up); the other entries point at an RTS ($2095, scroll_none). $1FAC copies the word into the operand of the call at $2063.
A lone RTS: the routine that the entries of the scroll table at $2075 for the directions without a scroll (0, 3, 7 and the unused ones) point at.
The fine horizontal scroll values for the four phases of a scroll to the right: 4, 2, 0, 6 (read by $209A).

Sets the fine horizontal scroll $1FA1 from the table at $2096 (4, 2, 0, 6) for the phase in $2070 and returns the phase in Y. When $1FA1 already holds that value, or when 10 or more steps are left ($206F) and $1FA1 is 0, it restores the camera X ($CB/$CC) from $1FAA/$1FAB and the player's X $7B16 from $5934 instead, so that step does not move the view. Called by $20C8, $2D14 and $326B.

Scroll direction 4, view to the right (entry 4 of the table at $2075). Moves the camera X ($CB/$CC) on 2 and the player's screen X $7B16 back 2, takes the fine scroll from $209A and runs the work of the phase it returns: phase 0 shifts the left columns of the screen one character left ($2117), 1 shifts the rest and draws the new right column ($2132), 2 builds the colours ($20FD), 3 copies the colours to colour RAM and flips the buffers ($2108).

Phase 2 of a scroll to the right: jumps to $459E when the buffer flag $1FA7 is 0 and to $3946 when it is 1. Both build the colour buffer from $71F4 (screen rows 10 to 18) from the matrix just made (from $C990 or $CD90 on) through the character colours at $BF00, and return to the caller of $20FD. Called from $20F5.

Phase 3 of a scroll to the right: $7131 fills colour RAM for screen rows 0 to 9 from the matrix just made, $68DA copies the buffer's rows 10 and 11 to colour RAM from $D990 and sets $68D9 so that the interrupt copies rows 12 to 18 ($6AB4), then the buffer flag $1FA7 is flipped so that the new matrix is shown. Called from $20F9.

Phase 0 of a scroll to the right: shifts columns 0 to $13 of the screen one character left into the other matrix, with $2153 (into $C800) when the buffer flag $1FA7 is 0 and $21CB (into $CC00) when it is 1. It first stores the loop limit $14 in the operand $21C7 or $223F. Called from $20E5.

Phase 1 of a scroll to the right: shifts columns $14 to $25 one character left into the other matrix ($2153 for $C800 when $1FA7 is 0, $21CB for $CC00 when it is 1, with the loop limit $26 stored in $21C7 or $223F) and then draws the new right column with $2243. Called from $20ED.

Copies the matrix at $CC00 one character to the left into $C800, 19 rows of 40, for the columns from Y up to the limit in the operand at $21C7: each pass copies column Y+1 of every row to column Y. Called from $2123 and $213E.
The loop limit of $2153: the operand of the CPY at $21C6 (the file holds $26). $2117 stores $14 here and $2132 stores $26.
Copies the matrix at $C800 one character to the left into $CC00, 19 rows of 40, for the columns from Y up to the limit in the operand at $223F. Called from $212E and $214C.
The loop limit of $21CB: the operand of the CPY at $223E (the file holds $26). $2117 stores $14 here and $2132 stores $26.

Draws the new right-hand column (column $26, 19 rows) of the matrix that is being made ($C800 when $1FA7 is 0, otherwise $CC00) from the level map. It reads 10 tiles down from the map pointer $A1/$A2 plus 20 columns, each as a two by two block through the tables $97F4 (top row) and $9892 (bottom row), taking the left or right character by the half-column flag $AF; when the half-row flag $BD is non-zero it starts with the bottom row of the first tile. Unless $2EC4 is set it then steps $AF on, adding 1 to the map pointer when it wraps. Called from $2141, $214F, $2DAE, $2DD0 and others.

Steps the half-column flag $AF on by one and, when it reaches 2, sets it to 0 and adds 1 to the map pointer $A1/$A2 (one tile to the right). Called by the diagonal scrolls to the right ($2DB1, $2DD3, $32D9, $32FB).
The fine vertical scroll values for the four phases of a scroll downwards: 4, 2, 0, 6 (read by $25F8).

Sets the fine vertical scroll $1FA2 from the table at $25F4 (4, 2, 0, 6) for the phase in $2070 and returns the phase in Y. When $1FA2 already holds that value, or when 10 or more steps are left ($206F) and $1FA2 is 0, it restores the camera Y ($D9/$DA) from $1FA8/$1FA9 and the player's Y $7B17 from $5935 instead. Called by $2626 and the diagonal scrolls that move down ($30B8, $3268).

Scroll direction 1, view downwards (entry 1 of the table at $2075). Moves the camera Y ($D9/$DA) on 2 and the player's screen Y $7B17 back 2, takes the fine scroll from $25F8 and runs the phase's work: 0 shifts columns 0 to $10 up a row and draws the new bottom row ($2691), 1 shifts columns $11 to $26 ($2676), 2 builds the colours ($265C), 3 copies the colours and flips the buffers ($2667).

Phase 2 of a scroll downwards: jumps to $459E when the buffer flag $1FA7 is 0 and to $3946 when it is 1, which build the colour buffer from $71F4 from the matrix just made (the same as $20FD). Called from $2654.

Phase 3 of a scroll downwards: fills colour RAM rows 0 to 9 ($7131), copies rows 10 and 11 of the colour buffer and asks the interrupt for rows 12 to 18 ($68DA), then flips the buffer flag $1FA7 (the same as $2108). Called from $2658.

Phase 1 of a scroll downwards: shifts columns $26 down to $11 of the screen up one row into the other matrix, with $26B2 (into $C800) when $1FA7 is 0 and $2724 (into $CC00) when it is 1. It first stores the loop limit $10 in the operand $2720 or $2792. Called from $264C.

Phase 0 of a scroll downwards: shifts columns $10 down to 0 up one row into the other matrix ($26B2 into $C800 when $1FA7 is 0, $2724 into $CC00 when it is 1, with the loop limit $FF stored in $2720 or $2792) and then draws the new bottom row into it ($2885 for $C800, $2796 for $CC00). Called from $2644.

Copies the matrix at $CC00 up one row into $C800, 18 rows, for the columns from Y down to the limit in the operand at $2720: row 0 of the column comes from row 1, and so on to row 17 from row 18. Called from $2682 and $269D.
The loop limit of $26B2: the operand of the CPY at $271F (the file holds $FF). $2691 stores $FF here and $2676 stores $10.
Copies the matrix at $C800 up one row into $CC00, 18 rows, for the columns from Y down to the limit in the operand at $2792. Called from $268D and $26AB.
The loop limit of $2724: the operand of the CPY at $2791 (the file holds $FF). $2691 stores $FF here and $2676 stores $10.

Draws the new bottom row (row 18) of tiles from the level map into the matrix at $CC00. The map position is the pointer $A1/$A2 plus $0280 (ten tile rows), plus 1 when the half-column flag $AF plus 1 reaches 2, stored in $93/$94; $2B30 gets that half-column state and $2B2F the half-row state $BD minus 1 (1, with the position moved 64 tiles back, when that is negative). $2B2F picks the character table $97F4 (0) or $9892, whose address is stored in the operands of the five loads below ($280D, $2814, $2845, $2855, $285C and the byte after each). It writes 40 characters from $CED0, or 39 when $2B30 is 1 (the second character of the first tile first). Unless $2EC4 is set it then steps $BD on, adding $40 to the map pointer when it wraps. Called from $26AE, $3151 and $3301.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $280C (high byte at $280E), rewritten by $2796 ($27D3-$27FB) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2813 (high byte at $2815), rewritten by $2796 ($27D3-$27FB) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2844 (high byte at $2846), rewritten by $2796 ($27D3-$27FB) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2854 (high byte at $2856), rewritten by $2796 ($27D3-$27FB) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $285B (high byte at $285D), rewritten by $2796 ($27D3-$27FB) with $97F4 or $9892.
The same as $2796 for the matrix at $C800: draws the new bottom row from $CAD0, and its table address operands are $28FC, $2903, $2934, $2944 and $294B. Called from $26A0, $312F and $32DF.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $28FB (high byte at $28FD), rewritten by $2885 ($28C2-$28EA) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2902 (high byte at $2904), rewritten by $2885 ($28C2-$28EA) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2933 (high byte at $2935), rewritten by $2885 ($28C2-$28EA) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2943 (high byte at $2945), rewritten by $2885 ($28C2-$28EA) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $294A (high byte at $294C), rewritten by $2885 ($28C2-$28EA) with $97F4 or $9892.

Steps the half-row flag $BD on by one and, when it reaches 2, sets it to 0 and adds $40 to the map pointer $A1/$A2 (one row of 64 tiles down). Called by the diagonal scrolls ($2DB4, $2DD6, $2F65, $2F87 and others).
The fine vertical scroll values for the four phases of a scroll upwards: 2, 4, 6, 0 (read by $2991).

Sets the fine vertical scroll $1FA2 from the table at $298D (2, 4, 6, 0) for the phase in $2070 and returns the phase in Y. When $1FA2 already holds that value, or when 10 or more steps are left ($206F) and $1FA2 is 6, it restores the camera Y ($D9/$DA) from $1FA8/$1FA9 and the player's Y $7B17 from $5935 instead. Called by $29BF, $2D14 and $2EC5.

Scroll direction 2, view upwards (entry 2 of the table at $2075). Moves the camera Y ($D9/$DA) back 2 and the player's screen Y $7B17 on 2, takes the fine scroll from $2991 and runs the phase's work: 0 shifts columns 0 to $10 down a row and draws the new top row ($2A2A), 1 shifts columns $11 to $26 ($2A0F), 2 builds the colours ($29F5), 3 copies the colours and flips the buffers ($2A00).

Phase 2 of a scroll upwards: jumps to $459E when the buffer flag $1FA7 is 0 and to $3946 when it is 1, which build the colour buffer from $71F4 from the matrix just made (the same as $20FD). Called from $29ED.

Phase 3 of a scroll upwards: fills colour RAM rows 0 to 9 ($7131), copies rows 10 and 11 of the colour buffer and asks the interrupt for rows 12 to 18 ($68DA), then flips the buffer flag $1FA7 (the same as $2108). Called from $29F1.

Phase 1 of a scroll upwards: shifts columns $26 down to $11 of the screen down one row into the other matrix, with $2A4B (into $C800) when $1FA7 is 0 and $2ABD (into $CC00) when it is 1. It first stores the loop limit $10 in the operand $2AB9 or $2B2B. Called from $29E5.

Phase 0 of a scroll upwards: shifts columns $10 down to 0 down one row into the other matrix ($2A4B into $C800 when $1FA7 is 0, $2ABD into $CC00 when it is 1, with the loop limit $FF stored in $2AB9 or $2B2B) and then draws the new top row into it ($2C17 for $C800, $2B31 for $CC00). Called from $29DD.

Copies the matrix at $CC00 down one row into $C800, 18 rows, for the columns from Y down to the limit in the operand at $2AB9: row 18 of the column comes from row 17, and so on to row 1 from row 0. Called from $2A1B and $2A36.
The loop limit of $2A4B: the operand of the CPY at $2AB8 (the file holds $FF). $2A2A stores $FF here and $2A0F stores $10.
Copies the matrix at $C800 down one row into $CC00, 18 rows, for the columns from Y down to the limit in the operand at $2B2B. Called from $2A26 and $2A44.
The loop limit of $2ABD: the operand of the CPY at $2B2A (the file holds $FF). $2A2A stores $FF here and $2A0F stores $10.

Set by the row drawing routines $2796, $2885, $2B31 and $2C17 to the half-row state of the row they draw (the half-row flag $BD minus 1, or 1 when that is negative): 0 picks the character table $97F4 (top characters of the tiles), 1 picks $9892 (bottom characters).

Set by the row drawing routines $2796, $2885, $2B31 and $2C17 to the half-column state of the row they draw (the half-column flag $AF plus 1, or 0 when that reaches 2): 0 builds the row from the first character of the first tile, 1 starts with its second character and ends one character earlier.

Draws the new top row (row 0) of tiles from the level map into the matrix at $CC00. The map position is the pointer $A1/$A2, plus 1 when the half-column flag $AF plus 1 reaches 2, stored in $93/$94; $2B30 gets that half-column state and $2B2F the half-row state $BD minus 1 (1, with the position moved 64 tiles back, when that is negative). $2B2F picks the character table $97F4 (0) or $9892, whose address is stored in the operands of the five loads below ($2BA3, $2BAA, $2BD9, $2BE9, $2BF0 and the byte after each). It writes 40 characters from $CC00, or 39 when $2B30 is 1. Unless $2EC4 is set it then steps $BD back, subtracting $40 from the map pointer when it goes below 0. Called from $2A47, $2DD9 and $2F8A, and by $3086 in the dead copy at $3075.

Not a routine entry: the operand of the call at $2063 as the file stores it ($2B67), which $1FAC overwrites from the table at $2075 before the call is made (the similar calls at $1222 and $5958 hold $128B and $5C49 in the file). Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2BA9 (high byte at $2BAB), rewritten by $2B31 ($2B69-$2B91) with $97F4 or $9892.

Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2BEF (high byte at $2BF1), rewritten by $2B31 ($2B69-$2B91) with $97F4 or $9892.
The same as $2B31 for the matrix at $C800: draws the new top row from $C800, and its table address operands are $2C89, $2C90, $2CBF, $2CCF and $2CD6. Called from $2A39, $2DB7 and $2F68.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2C88 (high byte at $2C8A), rewritten by $2C17 ($2C4F-$2C77) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2C8F (high byte at $2C91), rewritten by $2C17 ($2C4F-$2C77) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2CBE (high byte at $2CC0), rewritten by $2C17 ($2C4F-$2C77) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2CCE (high byte at $2CD0), rewritten by $2C17 ($2C4F-$2C77) with $97F4 or $9892.
Low byte of the table address in the instruction at $2CD5 (high byte at $2CD7), rewritten by $2C17 ($2C4F-$2C77) with $97F4 or $9892.

Steps the half-row flag $BD back by one and, when it goes below 0, sets it to 1 and subtracts $40 from the map pointer $A1/$A2 (one row of 64 tiles up). Called by the diagonal scrolls ($2DAB, $2DBA, $2DCD, $2DDC, $2F5C and others).

Scroll direction 6, view to the right and upwards (entry 6 of the table at $2075).
