"GAME OVER" in screen codes, ended by $FF; written by $587B at $CD50.

The player's state: 1 standing or walking, 2 falling, 3 jumping, 4 climbing, 5 punching, 6 crouching, 7 a strike. Read by $5936 and $6121, and by the strike $5A4F and the jump $5F2B, which test it for state 1 after landing.

Table of the eight state routines, one word each, indexed by the player's state $5923: 0 $5961 player_state_none (an RTS), 1 $5C49 player_walk, 2 $5E1C player_fall, 3 $5F2B player_jump, 4 $5B42 player_climb, 5 $59F1 player_punch, 6 $5BBF player_crouch, 7 $5A4F player_strike. $5936 copies the word into the operand of the call at $5958.
The player's screen X ($7B16) before this frame's move, saved by $5936 and $1FAC.
The player's screen Y ($7B17) before this frame's move, saved by $5936 and $1FAC.

Called from the top interrupt at $64F8 each frame, except while the banner flag $56A1 is set (the interrupt then jumps from $64D3 to $6552 past the call). Unless the game is paused ($6449) it saves the player's screen position in $5934/$5935 and runs the routine for the player's state $5923 (table at $5924, through a call whose operand is rewritten at $5959/$595A); it then draws the player's frames with $6121, also while paused.
Low byte of the address in the JSR at $5958 (high byte at $595A), rewritten by $594F and $5955 with the routine for the player's state from the table at $5924.
Scratch of $7A9C: the low byte of the 16-bit value it works on (camera minus a constant, plus the player's position), shifted right with the high byte $5960.
Scratch of $7A9C: the high byte of the 16-bit value it works on, shifted right 4 times (across) or 3 times (down) by $7A9C.
A lone RTS: the routine of player state 0 (entry 0 of the table at $5924), which does nothing.
Index of the current walk or climb frame, stepped by $5988, $59A9, $6056 and $6077.
The 18 sprite pointer values of the left-facing walk ($9D to $A2, three each), read by $5988 and $5C49.
The 18 sprite pointer values of the right-facing walk ($97 to $9C, three each), read by $59A9 and $5C49.
Toggled by $5988, $59A9, $6056 and $6077 so that the frame index advances on every second call.
Steps the left-facing walk animation: toggles $5987 and, on every other call, advances the index $5962 through the 18 frames at $5963, and on every call puts the frame in $611D. Called by $5C49.
The same for the right-facing walk: advances $5962 through the 18 frames at $5975 and puts the frame in $611D. Called by $5C49.
1 when the player faces left, 0 when he faces right.
The map column under the player (the Y that $7A9C returns), kept by $5C49 at $5D02 for the ladder tests at $5D23.
Sets the three sprite pointers in $611E, $611F and $6120 for the punch: $90, $B4, $BE when the player faces right ($59CA zero) and $91, $B5, $BF when he faces left. Called by $59F1 and $5C49.

Player state 5, punching (entry 5 of the table at $5924). While the punch timer $5C48 is non-zero it counts it down each frame and sets the punch frames through $59CC. When it has run out the state holds until fire ($1FA4 bit 4) is released, then returns to state 1 with the punch delay $5B40 set to 6.
Sets the three sprite pointers in $611E, $611F and $6120 for the strike: $8C, $A3, $B0 when the player faces right and $8D, $B1, $BB when he faces left. Called by $5A4F, $5BBF, $5C49 and $5F2B.

Table of the 13 height steps of state 7, -6 up to +6, read by $5A4F through the index $5F29. They are written as signed 16-bit values, but $5A4F adds only the first byte of each pair to the 8-bit height $7B17, so the second bytes are never read.

Player state 7, a strike or hop (entry 7 of the table at $5924). Adds the next step of the table at $5A35 (indexed by $5F29, two bytes a step) to the player's height $7B17; when the table is used up, or from index $0F on when the tile below is solid, it returns to state 1 (strike timer $5B3D and crouch flag $5B3E cleared, crouch delay $5B3F set to 10). It moves 2 pixels in the direction he faces ($59CA; left through $80AF, right through $8118): facing left, a blocker or the map's left end (map X below $0072) sends him 2 pixels right instead, while facing right a blocker or the map's right end stops him, and a solid tile puts his X back from $5934; puts frame $9B or $A1 in $611D and counts the strike timer $5B3D down with the strike frames ($5A10), setting the strike delay $5B3C to 10 when it runs out.
Set to 10 by $5A4F and $5F2B when the strike timer $5B3D runs out and counted down by them while it is zero. Nothing else in the traced code reads it.
Frames left of the strike; the hit test $1076, $6121 and $644A read it.
Non-zero while the player is crouching, and through a strike begun from a crouch ($5BBF does not clear it; the strike's end does). $6121 and the contact test $53D7 read it.
Delay before the player can crouch or strike from state 1: set to 10 when a strike or a crouch ends, to 4 when a climb ends and to 0 when a jump ends; counted down by $5C49.
Frames before the next punch can start: set to 6 when a punch ends ($59F1) and counted down by $5C49.
Delay before the next jump can start: set to 10 on every frame of a climb ($5B42) and counted down by $5C49, which starts a jump only when it is zero.

Player state 4, climbing (entry 4 of the table at $5924). Sets the jump delay $5B41 to 10. With up held ($1FA4 bit 0) it takes 1 off the player's height $7B17, sets the climb direction $603D to 1 and steps the frame with $6056; with down held (bit 1) it adds 1, sets $603D to 0 and steps the frame with $6077. It then looks at the tile one row below ($7A9C): while that is the ladder tile $0E or $0D the state stays 4. Otherwise it returns to state 1, sets the crouch delay $5B3F to 4, puts the standing frame $9A (facing right) or $A0 (left) in $611D and, if $603D is 1, adds 2 to the height $7B17.

Player state 6, crouching (entry 6 of the table at $5924). Fire ($1FA4 bit 4) starts a strike: state 7, index $5F29 cleared, strike timer $5B3D set to $0E, strike frames ($5A10) and sound effect 0 through $B0EE. With down released it returns to state 1 with the crouch delay $5B3F set to 10 and the crouch flag $5B3E cleared. While down is held, left and right turn him ($59CA) unless the recoil $1725 is running, and the crouch frames ($5C23) are set either way.
Holds the Y register saved by $5BDB: the immediate operand of the LDY at $5BE3.
Holds the X register saved by $5BD8: the immediate operand of the LDX at $5BE5.
Sets the three sprite pointers in $611E, $611F and $6120 for the crouch: $92, $B6, $C0 when the player faces right and $93, $B7, $C1 when he faces left. Called by $5BBF and $5C49.
Frames left of the punch; the hit test $1076, $6121 and $644A read it.

Player state 1, standing and walking (entry 1 of the table at $5924). Counts down the jump delay $5B41, clears the hit flags $1074/$1075 and the strike timer $5B3D, then moves 2 pixels left or right from the joystick $1FA4 (bits 2 and 3): it sets the facing $59CA, steps the walk animation ($5988, $59A9) unless the recoil $1725 runs, and is stopped by a blocker ($80AF, $8118), by the ends of the map (map X $1EA0/$1EA1 below $0072 or from $0398 on) and by a solid tile (1 to $0C; the player's X is put back from $5934). It then goes to state 2 when the tile below is empty or $0E and up, and otherwise starts a climb (state 4: up held with the ladder tile $0E at the player's column, or down held with the ladder-top tile $0D below while the area trigger flag $1F69 is clear), a jump (up held, state 3, when $5B41 is zero), a strike (down and fire, state 7) or a crouch (down, state 6) when $5B3F is zero, a punch (fire, state 5, when $5B40 is zero), or with the stick centred shows the standing frame ($5E09).
Holds the Y register saved by $5DA6: the immediate operand of the LDY at $5DAE.
Holds the X register saved by $5DA3: the immediate operand of the LDX at $5DB0.
Holds the Y register saved by $5DEB: the immediate operand of the LDY at $5DF3.
Holds the X register saved by $5DE8: the immediate operand of the LDX at $5DF5.
Puts the standing frame in $611D: $9A when the player faces right and $A0 when he faces left. Called by $5C49 and $5E1C.

Player state 2, falling (entry 2 of the table at $5924). Clears the hit flag $1074, moves left and right from the joystick as in state 1 (facing $59CA, blockers $80AF/$8118, map ends, solid tiles; no walk animation), then lowers him by 3 lines a frame (2 from line $82, none from line $97) and, when the tile below is 1 to $0D (solid or a ladder top), returns to state 1 with the standing frame ($5E09); otherwise it shows the falling frame ($5EC8).
Puts the falling frame in $611D: $7A when the player faces right and $7B when he faces left. Called by $5E1C.

Table of the 39 height steps of the jump, two bytes each, read by $5F2B through the index $5F29: from -4 at the start to +4 at the end. They are written as signed 16-bit values, but $5F2B adds only the first byte of each pair to the 8-bit height $7B17, so the second bytes are never read.
Index into the jump and strike height tables ($5EDB, $5A35), two bytes a step; cleared when a jump or a strike starts ($5C49, $5BBF) and stepped by $5F2B and $5A4F.
When non-zero, $6121 draws the player as in this state instead of the state in $5923; set to 1, 3, 6 or 0 by $5C49 and to 3 by $5F2B, and cleared by $6121 after use.

Player state 3, a jump (entry 3 of the table at $5924). Adds the next step of the table at $5EDB (indexed by $5F29) to the player's height $7B17. When the table is used up, or from index $29 on when the tile below is solid, it returns to state 1 (draw override $5F2A set to 3, strike timer $5B3D and crouch delay $5B3F cleared). It steers left and right from the joystick as in state 1 (facing $59CA, blockers $80AF/$8118, map ends, solid tiles), counts a running strike timer down with the strike frames ($5A10), and shows the jump frame ($602A).
Puts the jump frame in $611D: $F8 when the player faces right and $F9 when he faces left. Called by $5D59 when a jump starts and by $5F2B at the end of every frame of the jump.
1 while the player climbs up and 0 while he climbs down; set by $5B42 and by $5C49 when a climb starts, and read by $5B42 at the end of a climb.
Twelve sprite pointer values of the climb upwards ($94 to $96), indexed by $5962 in $6056.
Twelve sprite pointer values of the climb downwards ($94 to $96), indexed by $5962 in $6077.
Advances the climb frame upwards: toggles $5987 and, on every other call, steps $5962 through 12, and on every call puts the frame from the table at $603E in $611D. Called by $5B42.
Advances the climb frame downwards: toggles $5987, which decides whether $5962 steps on through 12, and on every call puts the frame from the table at $604A in $611D. Called by $5B42.
Fills with $FF the entries of the sorted sprite list at $0010 that each of the 11 slots used last frame (their positions are in $02-$0C). Called by the middle interrupt at $63BF.

Turns each slot's world position ($79/$B1 across, $95/$CD down) into a screen position by subtracting the camera ($CB/$CC and $D9/$DA): across into $87,X and $BF,X, down into $A3,X and $DB,X. A slot off the screen (X of $0150 or more, or height outside $23 to $C7) gets place 0; one on the screen goes to the first free place from its height / 2 in the list at $0010, and its place is kept in $02,X. Ends the list with $64 in $78. Called by the top interrupt at $64D6, before the multiplexer $66D5.
Sprite pointer value of the player's main frame, read by $6121 in every case but the punch, crouch and strike pictures, which come from $611E-$6120.
Sprite pointer for the player's sprite 2 while he punches, strikes or crouches; read by $6121.
Sprite pointer for the player's sprite 0 while he punches, strikes or crouches; read by $6121.
Sprite pointer for the player's sprite 1 while he punches, strikes or crouches; read by $6121.

Writes the player's three sprite pointers into both screens' tables ($CFF8-$CFFA and $CBF8-$CBFA). The state drawn is $5923, or the value in $5F2A when that is non-zero (which it then clears). For states 2 and 3 sprite 2 gets $611D, sprite 0 that plus 2 and sprite 1 that plus 4; for state 4 the pointers are $611D (sprite 2), plus $24 (sprite 0) and plus $2E (sprite 1); while the punch timer $5C48, the crouch flag $5B3E or the strike timer $5B3D is set they come from $611E (sprite 2), $611F (sprite 0) and $6120 (sprite 1), and otherwise sprite 0 gets $611D, sprite 1 that plus $0D and sprite 2 that minus $17. Called by $5936.

Called by the hit test $1076 (at $1142 and $11C5) with X the slot and Y the object. Takes 2 (when $1075 is set) or 1 from the object's energy $0BF8 and adds 4 to the score digit 5 ($5816); both calls in $1076 set $1075 just before, so it always takes 2. When the energy is already zero it instead sets the finale flag $621F and the timer $6221 to $16 for an object of variant 1 ($0C3E), and otherwise copies the slot's state to the object's counter $0B6C, sets the slot ($0ACC) and the object ($0B26) to state $10 and the next object's counter $0B6D to $FE. In both cases it then adds 8 to the score digit 5.
Holds the slot index saved by $61DE: the immediate operand of the LDX at $61E8.
Holds the slot index saved by $6212: the immediate operand of the LDX at $621C.
Set to 1 by $61BC when an object of variant 1 is beaten; while it is set $6313 stops reading the joystick and $93AF steers the player. Cleared by the setup.
Set to 1 by $93AF at the end of the finale; the main loop at $1F20 then shows the ending screen $75EA. Cleared by the setup.
Set to $16 by $61BC when the finale starts and counted down by $93AF; while it runs, objects 52 and 53 move down 1 pixel a frame.
Frames before the ending screen: $93AF starts it at $C8 once the player has reached map position $01BE and counts it down. Cleared by the setup.
Sprite pointers of behaviour $6271 for variant 0, indexed by the phase $0AA2 (0 to $1D): the shape $18 for phases 0 to 9, then 0 for the other twenty.

Sprite pointers $19, $1A and $1B, ten each, indexed by the phase $0AA2 of the previous slot: the frame $1DF5 gives a state 7 slot when the previous slot is in state $10. The extent is the run of the pattern.

Sprite pointers of behaviour $6271 for variant 1: the shape $18 for phases 0 to 5, then 0 for the next twelve (18 bytes in all). The phase can run to $1D, which would read the code after it; no variant 1 enemy gets here, since $61BC turns its defeat into the finale.

Behaviour for state $10 (entry 16 of the table at $124F), which $61BC gives an enemy whose energy has run out. Colour 9, multicolour. The next object's counter $0B6D, which $61BC sets to $FE, counts down by 1 on each update of the slot (update_objects $11D8 skips slots while paused or once the raster passes $B4); when it is zero the routine goes on into $62C2 and the enemy gets up again. The phase $0AA2 (which the hit test $1076 has just cleared) steps with that counter before the pointer is read: at $1E or more it counts up to $1D, below that down to 0. The pointer comes from $6223 (variant 0) by the phase, ten entries of the shape $18 then 0: the phase is 1 on the first update, so the enemy shows for nine updates, vanishes, and shows again for the last eleven before it gets up. Variant 1 would read $625F.

Reached by the branch at $627E from behave_knocked_down when the next object's counter $0B6D has counted down to zero. Sets the object's energy $0BF8 to 3 and gives slot and object their old state again: the counter $0B6C holds the state that $61BC saved there, which is always 1 or 2 (the state the hit test $1076 set just before); a value of 3 or more would have $0D taken off. It then sets the walking pointer: for state 1, $05 ($14 for variant 1); for state 2, $02 ($10 for variant 1). A knocked-down enemy gets up and walks again.
Sets the screen matrix bits of $D018 to $30 (screen at $CC00) when $1FA7 is zero and to $20 ($C800) when it is not, keeping the other bits. Called by the top interrupt at $64AF.

Raster interrupt 2 of 3 (vector $6313), on line $C5 (set by $6486). Saves A, X and Y in the operands at $63E6, $63E8 and $63EA, moves sprites 3-7 to line $0A, clears all sprite pointers $CFF8-$CFFF and $CBF8-$CBFF, turns the sprites off, clears the sprite multicolours $D025 and $D026, writes $D018 for screen $CC00 and ORs $4F into $D011 for the panel, and acknowledges the interrupt. It counts down the hurt guard $5447 and the recoil $1725, and reads $DC00 (joystick port 2) into $1FA4 and $DC01 (port 1 and the keyboard) into $1FA5 unless the recoil is still running while the hurt guard is zero, or the finale flag $621F is set. It sets the character set bits of $D018 to 8, runs the sprite list clear $6098, the timer $7B59 and the finale step $93AF, and toggles $63ED (counting $63EC down on every second frame). It sets line $CD and the vector $63EE for the next interrupt.
Holds the A register saved by irq_mid at $6313: the immediate operand of the LDA at $63E5.
Holds the X register saved by irq_mid at $6316: the immediate operand of the LDX at $63E7.
Holds the Y register saved by irq_mid at $6319: the immediate operand of the LDY at $63E9.
Counted down on every second frame by $6313 while it is not zero; nothing else in the traced code reads it.
Toggled between 0 and 1 by $6313 on every frame.

Raster interrupt 3 of 3 (vector $63EE), on line $CD (set by $6313). Saves A, X and Y in the operands at $6443, $6445 and $6447, ORs $2F into $D011 and $17 into $D016 and writes them back after 18 NOPs, which switches the status panel on (bitmap mode, multicolour), acknowledges the interrupt, sets raster line 0 and the vector $6486, clears bit 6 of $D011 and calls the scroll step $1FAC unless the banner flag $56A1 is set. It then restores A, X and Y and returns.
Holds the A register saved by irq_bottom at $63EE: the immediate operand of the LDA at $6442.
Holds the X register saved by irq_bottom at $63F1: the immediate operand of the LDX at $6444.
Holds the Y register saved by irq_bottom at $63F4: the immediate operand of the LDY at $6446.
1 while the game is paused ($74B1); the interrupts and routines skip the moving parts while it is set. Also set by the wipe $7413.

Moves sprite 0 ($D000) by 8 pixels along X while the punch timer $5C48 runs, or sprite 1 ($D002) while the strike timer $5B3D runs, to the right when the player faces right ($59CA zero) and to the left otherwise; does nothing when neither timer runs. Called by the top interrupt at $6523.

Raster interrupt 1 of 3 (vector $6486), on line 0 (set by $63EE). Saves A, X and Y in the operands at $656A, $656C and $656E, sets the fine scroll from $1FA1 ($D016) and $1FA2 ($D011), $D018 to $34, the screen ($62FD) and the multicolours. With the banner flag $56A1 set it calls $555F and goes to line $C5. Otherwise it sorts the sprites ($60C7), turns the sprites on unless the wipe flag $7411 is set, runs the first multiplexer pass ($66D5, limit $29), the player ($5936), places the player's sprites (X $7B16, Y $7B17) with $644A, makes sprites 0 and 1 white while the recoil $1725 is non-zero (colour 0 otherwise) and plays the sound ($B176). A second pass ($66D5, limit $8C), the colour copy $6AB4 and the object update $11D8 follow, then line $C5 and the vector $6313.
Holds the A register saved by irq_top at $6486: the immediate operand of the LDA at $6569.
Holds the X register saved by irq_top at $6489: the immediate operand of the LDX at $656B.
Holds the Y register saved by irq_top at $648C: the immediate operand of the LDY at $656D.

Busy-wait: the outer count is A and the inner count is A as well (Y and X both start from A), so the callers' values from $14 to $FF give delays from a few milliseconds to about a third of a second. Used by the wipe, the game over, continue, briefing and ending screens.
The first output of the step $6593: the entry of the table $657A at the index $65B8. Nothing reads it. The file holds 0.
Eight values read by $6593 by the index $65B8: $01, $0F, $0C, $0B, $00, $0B, $0C, $0F (they read as the C64 colours white, light grey, grey, dark grey, black and back up).
Eight values read by $6593 by the index $65B8 into $65BA: $01, $03, $0E, $06, $00, $06, $0E, $03 (white, cyan, light blue, blue, black and back up, if they are colours).
No caller: nothing calls, jumps to or branches to it. When the delay $65B9 is not zero it counts it down and returns; when it is zero it falls on into the step at $6593.

Entered only by falling through from $658A, which nothing calls. Sets the delay $65B9 to 3, steps the index $65B8 through 0 to 7 (back to 0 after 7) and copies the entry at that index of the three tables $657A, $6582 and $65BC to $6579, $65BA and $65BB. Nothing reads those three bytes.
Index 0 to 7 of the step $6593 into the three tables $657A, $6582 and $65BC. The file holds 0.
Delay of the step $6593: it sets it to 3 and $658A counts it down to zero before the next step. The file holds 0.
The second output of the step $6593: the entry of the table $6582 at the index $65B8. Nothing reads it. The file holds 0.
The third output of the step $6593: the entry of the table $65BC at the index $65B8. Nothing reads it. The file holds 0.
Eight values read by $6593 by the index $65B8 into $65BB: $09, $08, $0A, $07, $01, $07, $0A, $08 (brown, orange, light red, yellow, white and back, if they are colours).

Returns a pseudo-random byte in A. It stores the low three bits of CIA 1 timer A ($DC04) as the offset of the branch at $65D4, adds the timer's high byte ($DC05) to the seed $65E3, and rotates the sum left through the carry (set) by a number of places from 2 to 9 that the patched branch picks. The result is the new seed and the return value. Called by the behaviours at $18EB and $1B2F, which compare it with $14, and at $191A and $1B5E, which halve it into slot_walk $0AB0.

The offset of the BCS at $65D4, rewritten by $65C4 (at $65C9) with the low three bits of $DC04, so that the branch lands between $65D6 and $65DD in the chain of ROL instructions up to $65DE. The file holds $03.
The seed of $65C4: replaced by each result. The file holds $F1.
A lone RTS, called once per pass by the main loop at $1F02. The bytes after it ($65E5-$65F3) read $DD00 and would jump to $0810, but the traced code never reaches them.

Reads $DD00 (CIA 2 port A) and returns when bit 2 is set. When it is clear it removes three bytes from the stack (three PLA), disables interrupts and jumps to $0810. Nothing reaches it: the main loop calls $65E4, which is an RTS.
Fills the 1 KB screen matrix at $CC00-$CFFF with A. Called by the setup, the game over, continue, briefing and ending screens.
Fills colour RAM $D800-$DBFF with A. Called by the game over, continue, briefing and ending screens.

Key code read by $6619 and stored by $2067; cleared to 0 by the game over ($58AD), ending ($761C) and continue ($94BA) screens. $50 pauses ($74B1); $20, while the cheat flag $0A11 is set, runs the ending screen $75EA and ends the level (main loop at $1F30).

Reads the keyboard with CIA 1 into A. Returns $FF at once when any of the low five bits of $DC00 AND $DC01 reads low (the test at $6624, so while the joystick or a key in that range is down); otherwise scans the eight rows from $6690, looks the key up in the table at $6693 and returns its code (also keeping the table index in $02A7). $2067 keeps the result in $6618.
1 zero byte between read_keys ($6619-$668E) and key_row_select ($6690) ($668F), no reader.
The row select value written to $DC00 by $6619 while it scans the keyboard, rotated one bit for each row.
The number of the keyboard row $6619 is scanning.
The column bits read from $DC01 for the row being scanned by $6619.
Key codes for the 64 keys of the matrix, indexed by 8 times the column plus the row; $80 and above mean no code. Read by $6619.
Index into the sprite list at $0010 of the last slot the multiplexer handled; set to $10 by the top interrupt before each frame's first pass.
Raster line limit for the multiplexer: $29 for the first pass, $8C for the second.

Sprite multiplexer for sprites 3 to 7, called twice a frame by the top interrupt $6486 (with the raster limit $29 and then $8C in $66D4), and not at all while the banner flag $56A1 is set. Takes the next entry of the sorted sprite list at $0010 (position kept in $66D3, $64 ends the list) and, while the raster line is below the limit, gives it the next of the five sprites whose previous slot has finished (its height $15 lines or more above the raster): height into $D007, $D009, $D00B, $D00D or $D00F, X into $D006, $D008, $D00A, $D00C or $D00E with its ninth bit in $D010, the pointer $0A6A into both screens' tables ($CFFB-$CFFF and $CBFB-$CBFF), the colour $0A78 and the multicolour bit $0A86.

Bit masks for sprites 2 to 7 ($04, $08, $10, $20, $40, $80) followed by their complements ($FB, $F7, $EF, $DF, $BF, $7F). No code reads them: the multiplexer $66D5 and the interrupts use immediate masks.
Set to 1 by $68DA as it starts to copy rows 10 and 11 of the colour buffer; read and cleared by $6AB4, which then copies rows 12 to 18, and cleared by the setup $51F7 ($5268).

Copies the colours of screen rows 10 and 11 from the colour buffer to colour RAM: 39 colours of each row ($71F4-$721A to $D990-$D9B6 and $721C-$7242 to $D9B8-$D9DE, leaving out the last column of each), and sets the flag $68D9 so that the top interrupt copies rows 12 to 18 through $6AB4. Called by the finish phase of every scroll ($2108, $2667, $2A00, $2D6D and the others).

When the flag $68D9 is set, clears it and copies the colour buffer $7244-$735A to colour RAM $D9E0-$DAF6 (screen rows 12 to 18, 39 characters in each, leaving out the last column of each row); otherwise returns at once. Called every frame by the top interrupt at $654C, except while the banner flag $56A1 is set.
Last part of the copy of the colour buffer $7244-$735A to colour RAM: screen rows 16, 17 and 18, 39 colours each, from $72E4, $730C and $7334 to $DA80, $DAA8 and $DAD0, ending with the RTS at $7125.

No caller: nothing calls or jumps to it. Jumps to colour_buffer_from_cc ($3946) when the buffer flag $1FA7 is non-zero and to colour_buffer_from_c8 ($459E) when it is zero; the phase 2 routines of the scrolls make the same choice themselves.

Fills colour RAM rows 0 to 9 ($D800-$D98F, and $D990, the first byte of row 10, since Y starts at $28) from the matrix just made: for each column Y from $28 down to 0 and each of the 10 rows it looks up the colour of the character in the colour table $BF00. It reads $C800 when the buffer flag $1FA7 is 0 and $CC00 when it is 1. Called by the finish phase of every scroll ($2108, $2667, $2A00 and others), just before $68DA, which writes $D990 again.

Colours for screen rows 10 and 11, 40 bytes a row (80 bytes), built from the screen matrix by $3946 and $459E (columns 0 to 38 of each row; the last byte of each row is never written) and copied to colour RAM from $D990 by $68DA. Rows 12 to 18 follow at $7244.
Colours for screen rows 12 to 18, 40 bytes a row, one for each character; $6AB4 copies 39 of each 40 to colour RAM from $D9E0. The extent is what $6AB4 reads.
121 zero bytes between colour_buffer ($7244-$735A) and wipe_lengths ($73D4) ($735B-$73D3), no reader.
Lengths of the 56 diagonal lines of the wipe in $7413.
Two bytes ($01, $00) after the 56 lengths in $73D4 that $7413 does not read.
Characters still to clear on the diagonal line $7413 is drawing: loaded from $73D4 and counted down until it is zero.
Low byte of the start address of the diagonal line $7413 is drawing in screen B.
High byte of the start address of the diagonal line $7413 is drawing in screen B.
Set to 1 by $7413 and cleared by the setup; while it is set the top interrupt $6486 does not turn the sprites on.
1 zero byte between wipe_flag ($7411) and screen_wipe ($7413) ($7412), no reader.

Wipes the screen: sets the wipe flag $7411 and the pause flag $6449, then clears both screen matrices ($CC00 and $C800) in 56 diagonal lines, each stepping 39 characters from its start with the lengths taken from $73D4, a delay through $6570 after each, and clears the pause flag at the end. The first 40 lines start along the top row (columns 0 to 39), the last 16 down the right edge. Called by the game over screen $587B and the ending screen $75EA.
Holds the line number saved by $7460: the immediate operand of the LDX at $746B.
Holds the Y register saved by $7463: the immediate operand of the LDY at $746D.
Pause: when the key code in $6618 is $50, sets $6449, waits for the key to be released, pressed again and released, then clears $6449. Called by the main loop at $1F1D.

Types the ending text from $756B on the screen one character at a time, from $CC56, with a delay through $6570 after each: adds $66 to each code (a space becomes 0), $FF ends a line (the pointer moves on 2 rows) and a second $FF ends the text, which then waits for fire (bit 4 of $DC00), sets $9464 to 1 and runs two long delays. It first waits, clears the screen and fills colour RAM with 7. Called by the ending screen $75EA.
Holds the Y register saved by $7509: the immediate operand of the LDY at $7511.

The ending text in screen codes (letters as 1 to 26, doubled spaces as in the briefing): game completed, Strack falls to his doom, Darkman rescues his true love, "end of line". Each line ends with $FF and a second $FF ends the text; typed by $74D8.

The ending screen, called by the main loop at $1F25 when the ending flag $6220 is set or when $0A11 is set and the key code $6618 is $20. Runs the wipe $7413, stops the sound ($B828), switches to the text screen, swaps the character shapes ($9670), clears the screen, types the ending text through $74D8, waits one long delay and puts the shapes back.
The 70 starting types of the objects, copied to obj_type $0B26 by $7A1D (the 14 tables from $7649 to $7A1C are 70 bytes apart).
The 70 starting values of obj_counter $0B6C, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_flag $0BB2, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_energy $0BF8, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_variant $0C3E, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_flag_b $0C84, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_left_lo $0CCA, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_left_hi $0D10, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_right_lo $0D56, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_right_hi $0D9C, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_x_lo $0DE2, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_x_hi $0E28, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_y_lo $0E6E, copied by $7A1D.
The 70 starting values of obj_y_hi $0EB4, copied by $7A1D.

Copies the 70 entries of the 14 object tables from the level data at $7649-$7A1C into the working tables $0B26-$0EF9 (type, counter, flag, energy, variant, second flag, left and right limits, X and Y), clears the slot links $0F08 and the active flags $101A, and zeroes the 14-byte slot tables $0A94, $0AB0, $0ABE, $0ACC, $0EFA and $11CA. Called once by the setup $51F7 at $530D.

Finds the player's place in the level map for the player state routines ($5A80, $5AFA, $5B7A, $5CEE, $5CFF, $5E7E, $5EAB, $5F5A and $5FE5). Y becomes the map column: (camera X $CB/$CC minus $86 plus the player's X $7B16) divided by 16, minus 1; the sum before the division is left in $1EA0/$1EA1. X becomes twice the map row: (camera Y $D9/$DA minus $AE plus the player's Y $7B17) divided by 8, with bit 0 cleared; it picks a word in the table at $7EF7, which is stored in $E9/$EA as the address of that row of the map. Uses $595F/$5960 as scratch.
The player's screen X (sprite coordinates), $74 at the start; sprites 0, 1 and 2 are placed at this X by $6486, and the scroll routines change it.
The player's screen Y, $82 at the start; sprites 0 and 2 are placed at it and sprite 1 21 lines below.
Units digit of the timer; the timer is $7B18 (units), $7B19 (tens) and $7B1A (hundreds), counted down by $7B59 and drawn by $7B1B.
Tens digit of the timer (see $7B18).
Hundreds digit of the timer (see $7B18); the setup sets it to 5 when $0A10 is set and to 0 otherwise.
Draws the three timer digits into the panel's character shapes at $F9D8 (hundreds, $7B1A), $F9E8 (tens, $7B19) and $F9F0 (units, $7B18) through $7B43. Called by the main loop at $1F1A.
Copies the 8-byte shape of the timer digit $7B18+X from $1EA2 to the pointer $85/$86. Called three times by $7B1B.
Alternates 1 and 0 on each call of $7B59 that gets past its tests (not paused, digits not all zero); $7B59 counts the timer down only when it finds 0.

Called by the middle interrupt $6313 at $63C2 every frame; does nothing while the game is paused ($6449). When the three timer digits $7B18-$7B1A are zero it clears $0A10 and sets the timer state $7BCC to 1; otherwise on every second call ($7B58 alternates 1 and 0) it counts the digits down by one, the units first.
Called by the main loop at $1F17. When the timer state $7BCC is 1 it sets it to 2 and runs $7C36, which replaces the timer's picture in the panel; in any other state it does nothing.

Set to 1 by $7B59 on every unpaused frame while the timer digits read 000 (from the start of the level when $0A10 is clear, since the timer then starts at 000); $7BBB then steps it to 2 and redraws the panel picture, so this repeats on every main-loop pass. Nothing sets it to 0 (the file holds 2).

Copies the panel's timer picture for a running timer: five rows of 48 bytes from $7DCB, $7DFB, $7E2B, $7E5B and $7E8B to the bitmap at $F8C0, $FA00, $FB40, $FC80 and $FDC0, then five rows of 6 bytes from $7EBB, $7EC1, $7EC7, $7ECD and $7ED3 to colour RAM $DB18, $DB40, $DB68, $DB90 and $DBB8, and five from $7ED9, $7EDF, $7EE5, $7EEB and $7EF1 to the screen matrix at $CF18, $CF40, $CF68, $CF90 and $CFB8 (in the multicolour bitmap panel these bytes are colours, not character codes). Called by draw_panel ($53D2) when $0A10 is set.

The same copy as timer_graphics_on ($7BCD) with the picture for an expired or absent timer: rows of 48 bytes from $7C9F, $7CCF, $7CFF, $7D2F and $7D5F, five 6-byte colour RAM rows from $7D8F, $7D95, $7D9B, $7DA1 and $7DA7 and five 6-byte screen-matrix rows from $7DAD, $7DB3, $7DB9, $7DBF and $7DC5 (colours in the multicolour bitmap panel), to the same panel places. Called by draw_panel ($53CC) when $0A10 is clear and by timer_expired ($7BC8).

The panel picture for an expired or absent timer: five rows of 48 bitmap bytes, then ten rows of 6 bytes (five colour RAM rows and five screen-matrix rows, which hold colours in the bitmap panel), copied by $7C36. The extent is what $7C36 reads.

The panel picture for a running timer, laid out like timer_picture_off ($7C9F): five rows of 48 bitmap bytes, then ten rows of 6 bytes (five colour RAM rows and five screen-matrix rows, which hold colours in the bitmap panel), copied by $7BCD. The extent is what $7BCD reads.

Table of 77 16-bit pointers to the map rows, the first one twice: entry k from 1 on is $8182 + 64 x (k - 1). It starts on an odd address because $7A9C reads the low byte from $7EF7,X and the high byte from $7EF8,X with X twice the map row. The last four entries (rows 72 to 75) point at $9382 on, which holds code and not map rows.
Six bytes after the last row pointer: 0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 4. No code reads them.

Draws the opening view: 9 rows of tiles from the map at $90C4 (64 bytes a row) into screen B from $CC29 (two text rows for each map row), each row as the right half of its first tile ($807D) and 19 whole tiles ($803F). It then copies the 38 characters at $8017 to $CC00, puts the code $2C at $CE58, $CE80, $CEA8 and $CED0, and sets the colour RAM at $D800-$DAFF from the colour table at $BF00 indexed by each character. Called once by the setup $51F7.
The tile row number that $7F97 passes in X; $803F and $807D keep it here and leave the bottom half of the tile out when it is 9.
The 38 screen codes that $7F97 copies to the first row of screen B ($CC00).
Two screen codes, $28 and $7D, right after the 38 of first_row_chars ($8017). The copy loop of $7F97 stops at $26 (38) characters, so nothing reads them.

Writes tile A as two by two characters at the screen pointer $ED/$EE: the top pair from the table at $97F4 and, unless the tile row in $8016 is 9, the bottom pair from $9892 to the row below; then moves the pointer on 2 characters. Keeps X and Y in the operands at $8079 and $807B. Called by $7F97.
Holds the X register saved by draw_tile at $803F: the immediate operand of the LDX at $8078.
Holds the Y register saved by draw_tile at $8045: the immediate operand of the LDY at $807A.

Writes only the right half of tile A at the screen pointer $ED/$EE: the top right character from $97F5 and, unless the tile row in $8016 is 9, the bottom right character from $9893 to the row below; then moves the pointer on 1 character. Keeps X and Y in the operands at $80AB and $80AD. Used by $7F97 for the first tile of each row.
Holds the X register saved by draw_tile_right_half at $807D: the immediate operand of the LDX at $80AA.
Holds the Y register saved by draw_tile_right_half at $8083: the immediate operand of the LDY at $80AC.

Tests whether a slot in state 7 (the follower behaviour $1DF5) stands in the player's way to the left. Returns A=0 at once when the resident flag $0A10 is non-zero. Otherwise it goes through slots $0A down to 0 in state 7 whose previous object's slot ($0F07,Y) is not in state $10 and returns A=1 when the slot's screen X $87,X (high byte $BF,X zero) is at or up to $13 left of the player's $7B16 and the player's $7B17 is at most $13 lines below, or $27 lines above, the slot's height $A3,X minus $15 (kept in $53D6); A=0 if no slot is. Called by the player states ($5AA9, $5C76, $5E28 and $5F83) before a step left.
A lone RTS right after the jump at $80EC in blocked_left: no branch, jump or call reaches it.

Second part of blocked_left ($80AF). Reached by the branch at $80E2 when the player's height $7B17 is less than the slot's height minus $15 (kept in $53D6): it gives up unless the difference is less than $28. From $80FB, which the first part also reaches, the slot counts only when its screen X high byte $BF is 0 and its screen X $87 is the player's $7B16 or less than $14 below it; it returns A=1 then and otherwise goes back to the slot loop at $80BD.

The same test as $80AF for a step to the right: returns A=1 when a slot in state 7 has its screen X at or up to $13 right of the player's $7B16 (same height test, with $53D6), otherwise A=0. Called by the player states ($5ACB, $5CBE, $5E56 and $5FB1).
A lone RTS right after the jump at $8155 in blocked_right: no branch, jump or call reaches it.

Second part of blocked_right ($8118). Reached by the branch at $814B when the player's height $7B17 is less than the slot's height minus $15 (kept in $53D6): it gives up unless the difference is less than $28. From $8164, which the first part also reaches, the slot counts only when its screen X high byte $BF is 0 and its screen X $87 is the player's $7B16 or more than the player's by less than $14 (it returns A=1 then); otherwise it goes back to the slot loop at $8126.

The level map: 72 rows of 64 tile numbers (0 to $3E), row r at $8182 + 64 x r (pointers in map_row_pointers). A tile number picks two characters of the top row from tile_top_chars ($97F4) and two of the bottom row from tile_bottom_chars ($9892), which $7F97 and the scroll routines draw two by two. Columns 58 to 63 are tile $0C in 68 rows, column 0 is $0C in 59 rows and column 1 in 60; rows 70 and 71 are all tile 5. This symbol covers the map from row 0 column 0 ($8182) to row 15 column 63 ($8581): of its 1,024 numbers, tile 0 333, tile $34 252, tile $0C 141.
The level map, from row 16 column 0 ($8582) to row 31 column 63 ($8981): of its 1,024 numbers, tile 0 531, tile $0C 144, tile 4 70.
The level map, from row 32 column 0 ($8982) to row 47 column 63 ($8D81): of its 1,024 numbers, tile 0 489, tile $0C 144, tile 4 120.
The level map, from row 48 column 0 ($8D82) to row 63 column 63 ($9181): of its 1,024 numbers, tile 0 421, tile $0C 144, tile 4 117.
The level map, from row 64 column 0 ($9182) to row 71 column 63 ($9381): of its 512 numbers, tile 2 128, tile 5 128, tile 0 83.

Called first by the walking and attack behaviours $1726, $185C, $196C and $1AA1, with the slot in X and its object in Y. Does nothing unless the finale flag $621F is set and the object's variant $0C3E is non-zero. Then it adds 3 to the slot's Y ($95/$CD), writes the result to the object's Y ($0E6E/$0EB4), and writes the slot's Y plus $15 to the Y of the next object ($0E6F/$0EB5). So once the finale has begun, a variant 1 enemy sinks 3 lines on each update of its slot (update_objects $11D8 skips updates while paused or late in the frame) and drags the object after it down with it.

Called by the middle interrupt $6313 at $63C5 every frame. While the finale flag $621F is set (by $61BC, when an object of variant 1 is beaten) it replaces the joystick byte $1FA4 with $F7 (right pressed) until the map position $1EA1/$1EA0 reaches $01BE and with $FF (nothing pressed) from then on; at that point it starts $6222 at $C8, counts it down and sets the ending flag $6220 when it reaches 1. While $6221 is non-zero it counts it down and adds 1 to the Y position of objects 52 and 53 ($0EA2/$0EE8 and $0EA3/$0EE9).

Writes the continue screen's texts "PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE" from $9465 at $CD49 and "CREDITS" from $947C at $CF8C, adding $66 to each code and turning $20 into 0 (each ends at $FF), then the digit of $0A12 at $CF94 and the digit of $9463 at $CE1C (both as $8A plus the digit). Called by $9494.
The countdown shown on the continue screen, from 9; counted down by $9494 and drawn by $9418.

Set to 1 by $96AB and $74D8 when they finish: after the text has ended and fire is pressed (each waits on bit 4 of $DC00), or in $96AB also when fire skips the rest of the typing. Nothing else in the traced code reads it.
"PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE" in screen codes, ended by $FF; written by $9418.
"CREDITS" followed by spaces in screen codes, ended by $FF; written by $9418, with the digit of $0A12 after it.
Set to 1 by $9494 when fire is pressed to continue; read by the main loop at $1F4C.

The continue screen, entered from the main loop at $1F49 when the energy is zero and $0A11 is clear, after the game over screen $587B, if $0A12 (the credits) is not zero. Sets up the text screen, clears the score digits $0A00-$0A06 and $0A10, swaps the shapes ($9670), draws the texts through $9418 and counts $9463 down from 9 with delays; fire (bit 4 of $DC00) takes one from $0A12 and sets the continue flag $9493 to 1, and when the count runs out the flag stays 0. Then puts the shapes back and redraws the panel ($53A6).
Character shapes (136 bytes) for the text screens, exchanged with $C338 by $9670.
Character shapes (136 bytes) for the text screens, exchanged with $C3C0 by $9670.
40 zero bytes between text_shapes_b ($95C0-$9647) and swap_shapes ($9670) ($9648-$966F), no reader.

Exchanges three blocks: 136 bytes at $9538 and 136 at $95C0 with $C338 and $C3C0, and the 80 bytes of digit shapes at $1EA2 with $C450. Called to put the text screens' shapes in and to restore the play shapes.
Counts down from $1E while $96AB or $74D8 types the first characters of the text; in the briefing fire is not tested during that time.
Index of the next character of the text that $96AB or $74D8 types.

Types the level briefing from $973F on the screen one character at a time, from $CC56, with a delay through $6570 before each: adds $66 to each code (a space becomes 0), $FF ends a line (the pointer moves on 2 rows) and a second $FF ends the text, which then waits for fire (bit 4 of $DC00). Fire is ignored for the first $1E passes of the loop ($96A9), which are 29 characters and the first line end; pressing it later skips to the end, where $9464 is set to 1 and two long delays run. It first waits, clears the screen and fills colour RAM with 7. Called by the setup $51F7; the setup calls $9670 before and after it.
Holds the Y register saved by show_briefing at $96E1: the immediate operand of the LDY at $96E9.
The level briefing in screen codes ("level six", Darkman pursues Strack to free his love and kill his creator, "end of line"); each line ends with $FF and a second $FF ends the text. Typed by $96AB.
The $FF that ends the last line of briefing_text ($973F). The second $FF, which ends the text for $96AB, is the first byte of tile_top_chars ($97F4).

For each tile (index times 2) the two screen codes of its top row; the characters count in strips of 40 across the character set. Read by $803F and $807D, by the scroll routines draw_right_column ($2243) and draw_left_column ($3599), and by the row routines $2796, $2885, $2B31 and $2C17. The extent is the pattern up to the bytes at $9872.
Three bytes, $60, $00 and $00, between tile_top_chars and unused_continue_text ($9875); nothing reads them.
"PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE" in screen codes, ended by $FF. This level's continue screen reads its own copy at $9465, and nothing in the traced code reads these bytes.

The six letters CREDIT in screen codes ($03 $12 $05 $04 $09 $14), right after unused_continue_text and before tile_bottom_chars ($9892); nothing reads them. The credits text that is drawn is credits_text ($947C).

For each tile (index times 2) the two screen codes of its bottom row, read by $803F and $807D, by the scroll routines draw_right_column ($2243) and draw_left_column ($3599), and by the row routines $2796, $2885, $2B31 and $2C17. The extent is the pattern up to the panel characters at $9914.

The 200 screen-matrix bytes of the status panel, copied to $CEF7 by $53A6. The panel is shown in multicolour bitmap mode, so each byte holds a cell's two colours, not a screen code. $CEF7 is row 18 column 39, so the first byte lands in the playfield and panel rows 19 to 23 take bytes 1 to 199.
The 200 colour RAM bytes of the status panel, copied to $DAF7 by $53A6. $DAF7 is row 18 column 39, so the first byte lands in the playfield and panel rows 19 to 23 take bytes 1 to 199.

92 bytes left in memory from an earlier program, not used by this level: nothing in the level's code refers to them. They are the second half of a keyboard reader (the instruction that stores the row select in $DC00 and the rest of the scan) and the first five bytes of its key table, the same bytes as level 4's $9AA4-$9AFF except at $9AF7-$9AF9, where level 4 keeps its keyboard variables. This level's own keyboard reader is read_keys ($6619).

Colour for each character code, indexed by the character; the colour buffer routines colour_buffer_from_cc ($3946) and colour_buffer_from_c8 ($459E) with their continuation parts, fill_colour_top ($7131), $7F97 and $56A5 read it to fill the colour RAM, and the setup $51F7 ORs $08 into every entry.
Pointer $00: 64 zero bytes, the empty frame. The text screens read their character set from $C000 ($D018=$30 in the setup $51F7), so these bytes are also character 0, the blank.

Sprite shapes for pointers $01 to $0B and the first 56 bytes of $0C (760 bytes). In use: $01 in the frame table $5476 (behaviour $548E); $02 and $03, an enemy walking right of variant 0 (table $1A61); $05 and $06, walking left (table $181C); $04 and $07, the frames at counter $0E of the attacks $196C and $1726 for variant 0; $08 to $0B, the frames of slot_follow below its limit (table $1E7F), and $0C, the first of its frames at or above the limit (follow_frames_high $1E5F).

136 bytes that $9670 swaps with text_shapes_a ($9538). On the text screens they are character shapes of the font; during play they are sprite data, the last 8 bytes of pointer $0C and all of $0D and $0E, which slot_follow shows through follow_frames_high ($1E5F).

136 bytes that $9670 swaps with text_shapes_b ($95C0). On the text screens they are character shapes of the font; during play they are sprite data: all of pointer $0F (follow_frames_high $1E5F), all of $10 and the first 8 bytes of $11, the frames of an enemy of variant 1 walking right (table $1A81).

8 bytes between the swapped letters (char_shapes_text_b) and the swapped digits (char_shapes_digits): the font's character 137, which $9670 leaves alone. During play they are bytes 8 to 15 of the sprite shape for pointer $11, the second frame of an enemy walking right of variant 1 (table $1A81).
The 80 bytes that $9670 exchanges with the digit shapes at $1EA2.

Sprite shapes from byte 32 of pointer $12 to the end of $1F (864 bytes). In use: $13 and $17, the attack frames of variant 1 at counter $0E ($196C and $1726); $14 and $15, walking left of variant 1 (table $183C); $18, the knocked-down frame of $6271 (tables $6223 and $625F); $19 to $1B, follow_frames_a ($6241); $1F in the frame table $5476.
Screen matrix A: 25 rows of 40 characters in text mode, written by the scroll routines. $D018 selects it, or screen_b, from screen_buffer ($1FA7) through $62FD.
16 zero bytes after the 25 rows of 40 characters of screen_a, between its last row ($CBE7) and its sprite pointers ($CBF8); the VIC does not display them.

The sprite pointers of screen A's table ($CBF8-$CBFF); the player's sprites 0 to 2 are written by $6121, sprites 3 to 7 by the multiplexer $66D5, and the banner's by banner_sprites ($555F) and banner_pointers ($5669, with its entry $5670); the middle interrupt $6313 sets all eight to 0 every frame. Always written together with sprite_pointers_b.
Screen matrix B: the same layout as screen_a, 25 rows of 40 characters. The briefing is typed into it at $CC56 and the game over text at $CD50; the panel is drawn into it by $53A6.
16 zero bytes after the 25 rows of 40 characters of screen_b, between its last row ($CFE7) and its sprite pointers ($CFF8); the VIC does not display them. fill_screen ($65F4) can overwrite them.

The sprite pointers of screen B's table ($CFF8-$CFFF); the player's sprites 0 to 2 are written by $6121, sprites 3 to 7 by the multiplexer $66D5, and the banner's by banner_sprites ($555F) and banner_pointers ($5669, with its entry $5670); the middle interrupt $6313 sets all eight to 0 every frame. These also write sprite_pointers_a; fill_screen ($65F4) clears this table alone when it fills screen B for the text screens.

Characters 0 to 127 of level 6's play character set (1,024 bytes, 8 bytes a character, one byte a pixel row). The top interrupt irq_top ($6486) stores $34 in $D018 at $64AC, which sets the character base to $D000 and the screen to $CC00; select_screen ($62FD) then switches the screen between $CC00 and $C800 and keeps the character bits. tile_top_chars ($97F4) and tile_bottom_chars ($9892) pick the codes, and char_colours ($BF00) gives each its colour. Level 4 has a different character set here (1,823 of the 2,048 bytes differ). Only the VIC sees these bytes: with the I/O area switched in, the CPU reads the chips' registers at the same addresses.

Characters 128 to 245 of the play character set (944 bytes), the same form as play_charset_a. The tiles the map uses put codes up to $F5 (tile_top_chars) and $FB (tile_bottom_chars) on the screen; the codes from $F6 up are the blank characters of play_charset_blank, and the $FC to $FF at the end of tile_bottom_chars belong to entries the map does not use. Only the VIC sees these bytes: with the I/O area switched in, the CPU reads the chips' registers at the same addresses.

Characters 246 to 255 (80 bytes), all zero: the blank characters. Sprite pointer $5F would read the last 64 of these bytes, and pointers $5A to $5E read other characters as sprite data, so $5A to $5F are not shapes.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $62 and $63 (128 bytes): the pickup of the behaviour at $1BBE, named by pickup_frames ($1BB0). A heart, the same size in both; $63 has a thicker outline.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $6D to $6F (192 bytes): rows of vertical bars at three heights, the flashing hazard of behaviour $16BA, named by flash_frames ($165E).

48 zero bytes after the shape for pointer $FE, up to the end of this level's file at $FFEF; no reader. The interrupt vectors at $FFFA-$FFFF lie past the file, and the level sets them itself.
